summary: newWorkflowArchiveCmd (internal/cli/channel_workflow.go) constructs a real `sync` command instance (newSyncCmd(flags)) with --resources workouts,classes (which cascades to performance/workout_details/classes_detail) plus its own --db/--full/--max-pages/--max-parents/--stale-before flags translated into sync args, and executes it via ExecuteContext rather than re-implementing sync's resource list, dependent fan-out, or bounding logic. It sets SilenceErrors/SilenceUsage on the detached sync instance so a failure doesn't print twice (once from the detached command's own Execute(), once when its error propagates back to the real root's Execute()). Any future change to sync's resource list, dependent cascade, or bounding semantics is automatically inherited here -- workflow_archive must keep delegating, never grow a second hand-rolled sync loop, or these two commands will silently diverge again. --max-pages bounds the flat workouts/classes phase; --max-parents alone does NOT bound it, since it only gates the per-workout dependent fan-out that runs after the flat phase completes -- both are needed together to keep a call inside an MCP tool timeout on an account whose classes resource (no incremental filter) has a large history. As of round 11, when PELOTON_MCP_SHELLOUT is set (see cliutil.MCPShelloutEnvVar -- set by cmd/peloton-pp-mcp on itself at startup and inherited by every companion CLI subprocess the MCP shellout layer spawns), an unset --max-pages/--max-parents default to 5/500 instead of staying unlimited, so an MCP agent that calls this tool with no arguments still gets a bounded call. A human shell invocation (the env var unset) keeps unbounded-by-default behavior. Any future regen must preserve this env-gated default, or an MCP-driven archive call with no explicit flags reverts to hanging on the flat classes phase.
reason: newWorkflowArchiveCmd's resource list was hardcoded to an empty slice (`resources := []string{}`), so every invocation -- with or without --full, --dry-run, or any flag -- silently reported {"resources_synced":0,"total_items":0} and archived nothing at all, on any account, confirmed live. This is also reachable as an MCP tool (`workflow` is one of the framework tool groups), so an agent calling it saw a clean success response for a command that never did anything. A round-9 report characterized this as "no bounding flags, same as pre-round-4 sync" and suggested adding --max-parents/--stale-before; investigation found the command was actually non-functional altogether, a materially worse defect than reported, which a minimal flag-only fix wouldn't have caught. User chose full delegation to sync's proven machinery over a second hand-rolled bounded loop or redirecting the command to fail with a pointer to sync. A round-10 report then found --max-parents alone insufficient: a real account's classes phase (48,742 items, no incremental filter) took ~4.5 minutes regardless of --max-parents, so no invocation could complete inside an MCP tool call's timeout. --max-pages closes that gap, but a round-11 report found the flag alone still wasn't enough in practice: the report's own repro call (`workflow_archive --max-parents 25 --json`) omitted --max-pages, and no MCP agent can be expected to already know about a flag it was never told to pass. The fix moves the burden from "the caller must know the magic flag" to "the command defaults safely when it can detect it's running as an MCP tool call."
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green. TestWorkflowArchiveActuallyArchivesData drives the real command end-to-end against a fake server and asserts all four cascaded resources (workouts, classes, performance, workout_details) end up populated, and that --json output matches sync's own event-stream shape rather than the old dead-command shape. TestWorkflowArchiveBoundingFlagsAccepted confirms --max-pages/--max-parents/--stale-before are real, wired flags. TestWorkflowArchiveMaxPagesBoundsFlatPhase drives a fake 3-page classes list and asserts --max-pages 1 stops after exactly 100 items (one page) with a max_pages_cap_hit warning. TestWorkflowArchiveDefaultsBoundedUnderMCPShelloutEnv drives the same never-terminating classes fixture with PELOTON_MCP_SHELLOUT set and NO --max-pages/--max-parents flags, and asserts the flat phase still hits a max_pages_cap_hit warning at the default cap of 5. Live-verified against the real account: --max-parents 5 alone (no --max-pages) still reported success=4/warned=0/errored=0 with classes fully paginated at 48,742 items in ~4.5 minutes; --max-pages 1 --max-parents 5 together completed the entire four-resource run (workouts, classes, performance, workout_details) in ~3.6 seconds, each flat resource correctly capped at 100 items with a max_pages_cap_hit warning and each dependent correctly capped at 5 with a max_parents_cap_hit warning.
